description:
FOUND s506f (Opus, 2026-10-04) by the -n line-number probe.  perl appends `, <FH> line N.` to a die/warn
location when a filehandle has been read (`$.` is live); PCL never does.

REPRODUCER (perl 5.40.3 vs PCL 618db500 and s506f):
  printf 'a\n' > one.txt
  perl -e 'my $l = <STDIN>; warn "w"' < one.txt   -> w at -e line 1, <STDIN> line 1.
  pcl  -e 'my $l = <STDIN>; warn "w"' < one.txt   -> w at -e line 1.
  printf 'a\nb\n' | perl -ne 'die "x" if $. == 2' -> x at -e line 1, <> line 2.
  (pcl: "x at -e line 1." -- plus the "While evaluating the form" wrapper, #2492)

perl's rule (Perl_mess_sv): when PL_last_in_gv is set and its IoLINES is non-zero, append
`, <NAME> line N` (`<>` for ARGV reading STDIN/files, `chunk` instead of `line` when $/ is not "\n").
Pre-existing, not switch handling: every program that reads a file and then dies shows it.  STDERR
only (the everyday battery compares STDOUT + status), but fresh_perl_is rows with 2>&1 compare it.
subject: die/warn locations lack perl's `, <FH> line N.` suffix after a filehandle read (`x at -e line 1, <> line 2.`)
